signals.classification: CONFIRMED FRESH CAPABILITY; DELAYED PRIMARY-SOURCE RECOVERY
signals.changed: Cloudflare added an Inspect panel to Browser Run Session Recordings with searchable console logs, network request and response details, timing waterfalls, HAR download, and an expandable final DOM snapshot. The recording API can also return raw JSON or HAR.
signals.free_value: The inspection and export capability has no separately announced charge. Workers Free includes 10 browser minutes per day and three concurrent browser sessions; recordings are retained for 30 days.
signals.approximate_value: No defensible cash equivalent. It replaces custom browser-agent instrumentation and turns a replay into an inspectable execution artifact suitable for debugging and evidence capture.
signals.cash_required: $0 within Workers Free allowances. Paid includes 10 browser hours per month, then $0.09 per additional hour; Browser Sessions also meter concurrency.
signals.eligibility_reality_check: Requires a Cloudflare account, Browser Run session through Puppeteer, Playwright, or CDP, and per-session recording opt-in. It is unavailable for Quick Actions. No company, funding, incorporation, geography, domain-email, or team-size gate.
signals.why_asymmetric: A single browser run can now yield replay, console evidence, network chronology, payload and response details, final DOM state, and a portable HAR without maintaining a second observability stack.
signals.catch: Network records can expose headers, payloads, responses, tokens, and personal data. Input fields are masked by default in the replay, but that does not establish network-level redaction. Recordings expire after 30 days, large or highly dynamic pages produce high event volume, and canvas, cross-origin iframes, media, and WebGL are not captured.
signals.window: Active beta; no expiry announced. Recordings themselves are retained for 30 days and are limited to two hours.
signals.immediate_exploit: Record one synthetic, nonproduction flow; close the session; export HAR and raw JSON; inspect logs, network data, and final DOM for secret leakage; then retain only a sanitized evidence bundle or digest in ICE.
